claims.text: Adding a minor amount of an element with a significantly larger atomic radius increases the alloy's overall atomic size mismatch relative to the baseline.
Increasing atomic size mismatch enhances local lattice distortion in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Enhanced local lattice distortion increases the energy barrier for dislocation motion.
A higher energy barrier for dislocation motion increases high-temperature yield strength.
Increased lattice distortion stiffens local bonds.
Stiffer local bonds produce more pronounced thermoelastic recovery upon unloading.
The modified alloy will have higher yield strength than the low-mismatch baseline at temperatures above approximately 800°C.
The modified alloy will show greater thermoelastic recovery than the baseline at high temperature.
Greater thermoelastic recovery will be manifested as a higher elastic modulus at high temperature.
Increased XRD peak broadening can serve as evidence of enhanced local lattice distortion.
More pronounced short-range-order variations observed by high-resolution TEM can serve as evidence of enhanced local lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism applies under mechanical loading above approximately 800°C in a controlled inert atmosphere.
Using an inert atmosphere excludes oxidation effects from the comparison.
Phase stability and subtle microstructural variations may compete with the proposed size-mismatch effects.
